newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end higher, warm weather limits gains.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end higher, warm weather limits gains.

text.p: NYCE frozen concentrated orange juice futures settled firmer and near the highs Tuesday, but prices remained firmly entrenched in their recent trading range.

Gains were stymied by a lack of fundamental news. While colder temperatures and the impending winter tend to buoy FCOJ prices during this time of year, warm weather across the Florida citrus belt has put a damper on any potential rally, market sources said.

Low temperatures during the next three to four days are expected to remain in the 50s (Fahrenheit). "There continues to be virtually no threat of any frost/freeze damage to the citrus during the next ten days," said Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis.
The January contract closed up 0.90 to 95.70, traded from 96.40 to 95.20. The back months finished 0.45 and 0.30 firmer.
On the charts, traders pegged near-term January support at 95.00 cents and then at 91.75 cents. Resistance was seen at 100.58 cents, the 40-day moving average.
